correctness.rationale: For any allowed finite reversal rate, each block of duration L/v has conditional probability at least exp(−λL/v) min(p,q) of absorption, giving a finite mean. The backward equations for dimensionless directional means give D'=−2 and S'=2zD, where D is their difference and S their sum. Writing D=1+c−2y and S=B+2z((1+c)y−y²), the transmitting survival boundaries at 0 and 1 reduce to pB+(p+2z)c=2−p and qB−[q+2(1−q)z]c=2−q. The determinant has nonzero magnitude 2H, H=pq+sz. Hence c=(q−p)/H and averaging S/2 gives B/2+z/6+zc/2, which simplifies to the stated mean. At z=0 this is (1/p+1/q−1)/2 as also obtained directly from the half-traversal mean plus repeated ballistic trials. Its derivative is 1/6−(p−q)²/(2H²). For unequal p,q the derivative strictly increases to 1/6; the minimum is interior exactly when the derivative at zero is negative, and is unique at zero at equality or below. At p=q the term with the squared difference is absent and the slope is strictly positive. The example gives z*=(3√3−1)/4 and T*=5/6+√3/4 with ballistic T=2. The positive p,q restriction is essential for the ballistic endpoint.
residual_risks: The finite-volume check is corroborative, not an all-parameter proof; no convergence rate or one-way-detector ballistic formula is asserted.

value.rationale: The result separates a ballistic regime from a tumbling-assisted one for a natural transparent point trap, and identifies the exact balance between directional asymmetry and the reaction probabilities. The optimum and its transition are testable predictions; they show why asymmetry alone does not suffice and why results with reflection cannot automatically be used. This applies throughout the stated range of both reaction probabilities, not only at the illustrative parameter choice.
residual_risks: No conclusion is established for multiple, extended or sticky traps, unequal speed magnitudes, position-dependent switching, or nonuniform initial laws.
